title: Colette UGC — Finally Got It Right

cards.text: COLETTE UGC — FINALLY GOT IT RIGHT

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: AIUGC ad, max 50s, 8 fixed 6s segments, same Creator A anchor and room as the fall-bag board. LAW: the Colette is on screen the ENTIRE runtime — the bag-graveyard and slump-prop visuals are BANNED and replaced with the Colette demonstrating the opposite while the VO dismisses the failed bags. Angle: serial bag disappointment; the Colette finally does everything. Verdict-led. Centerpiece is the pack-and-stand demo at 0:30 (8 seconds, no cutaway). Three frames queued for regen behind the kie top-up. Loro Piana line is an approved exception to the zero-reference rule for these ads only.
Fixed low-angle phone, creator on floor, bag in hand from second one

cards.text: credibility through setting, product never leaves her hands
Both hands working the bag toward the lens

SCRIPT
cards.text: Okay, if you've spent years trying to find the right bag, I need to show you something.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: REGEN QUEUED: creator leaning into the lens mid-sentence with the Colette held in her lap, both hands on it. No other bags anywhere

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
recognition — hook; calls out the serial searcher, ours already in hand

Replaces the banned graveyard frame. Blocked on kie top-up.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Every bag I've bought got one thing right and everything else wrong. The pretty ones collapsed the second I set them down, and the roomy ones had no shape at all.

cards.title: VISUAL
cards.text: REGEN QUEUED: she presses the Colette's side firmly and it springs back holding its shape, deadpan glance at camera. The failed bags exist ONLY in the VO

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
frustration spoken, superiority shown — ours visibly does what they couldn't

Replaces the banned slump-prop frame. Blocked on kie top-up.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: This is the one that finally got it right. The Colette from Velantra. It's obviously inspired by the Loro Piana wool tote, except that one is thousands of dollars and this is about a hundred and twenty.
Colette up beside her face, front face square to camera. Post overlay: $119.99

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
verdict — leads with the conclusion, price contrast lands the anchor

Uses the clean ANCHOR frame (the prior version had a prop tote in frame, now banned and deleted).

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Soft brushed wool, but with actual structure. It stands upright packed full or half empty.
Fingers denting the soft nap while the bag holds its form, pushed to the lens

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: surprise — the soft-but-structured paradox is the mechanism

cards.title: OUR VERSION — 8 segments, 50s · COLETTE IN EVERY FRAME

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: LAW — PRODUCT ALWAYS ON SCREEN
cards.text: The Colette is in every single frame. BANNED and deleted from this board: the bag-graveyard hook, the slump-prop beat, the collapsed-puddle cutaway, and the verdict frame that had a prop tote at the edge. Failed-bag lines are VO-only over footage of OURS demonstrating the opposite.

cards.title: REGEN QUEUE (blocked on kie top-up, balance 8.3)
cards.text: 1) Hook: Colette in her lap, leaning in. 2) Press-test beat: side pressed in, springs back. 3) Open-top detail: short gold-capped belt end (prior render failed QA on belt length). Fire all three the moment credits land, then re-push this board.

cards.title: ENGINES + VARIANTS
cards.text: Seedance 2.5 lipsync from these keyframes, all seeded from the shared ANCHOR, never chained. Omni animates cutaways. Text overlays in post. Creators B and C re-render this spine after approval; 3 AI-VO variants reuse the product beats with an ElevenLabs v3 continuous take.
